proposed.text: The contract documents package includes architectural drawings, structural drawings, mechanical drawings, electrical drawings, and plumbing drawings. Who is responsible for ensuring these documents are coordinated and integrated?

options.text: Each specialist is responsible only for their own drawings; coordination is the contractor's responsibility during construction
The architect, as the lead designer, typically coordinates the design and ensures all specialists integrate their work with the architectural design
The structural engineer, as the most technically senior professional, coordinates all design disciplines and resolves conflicts
No coordination is required if each professional signs and seals their respective documents independently

rationale.a: Misallocates responsibility; coordination is a design team function, not a contractor construction function.
rationale.c: Incorrectly designates the structural engineer as coordinator; the architect is the lead designer and coordinates all disciplines.
rationale.d: Falsely assumes professional seals eliminate coordination responsibility; coordination is essential and precedes sealing.
rationale.correct: Professional practice requires coordination of multi-disciplinary drawings. The architect typically serves as the lead designer (UAP SPP 202) and is responsible for facilitating coordination between the architect's design and the various engineering disciplines. Coordination ensures that structural elements fit within the architect's spatial design, that mechanical and electrical systems can be routed through available spaces, and that all elements integrate into a cohesive building. Failure to coordinate results in conflicts that create construction problems and cost overruns.
rationale.takeaway: The architect, as lead designer, is responsible for coordinating all design disciplines to ensure integrated, conflict-free contract documents.
